history.summary: Chamunda Devi Ji Temple is a small neighbourhood Devi shrine in the Shakti Vihar / Hazura Kapura Colony area (Minucha Colony, National Colony side) of Bathinda, rated about 4.4-4.6 stars in local listings. No source documents its history or founding - treat all such claims as UNVERIFIED. Do NOT confuse it with the famous Chamunda Devi Shakti Peeth temple in Kangra, Himachal Pradesh; image searches for 'Chamunda Devi Temple' return the Kangra temple, and no verified photograph of this Bathinda shrine could be found, so media is empty. Coordinates 30.2322, 74.9502 from geocoder, matching listing data.

name: Chamunda Devi Ji Temple
town_description: Bathinda is one of the oldest cities in Punjab's Malwa region, historically associated with the 1000 AD-era Qila Mubarak fort and the Razia Sultan legend. It is a major railway junction and a commercial centre for the region's cotton and food-grain trade, sometimes called the 'City of Lakes'. The temple is in the Hazura Kapura Colony / Shakti Vihar neighbourhood of the city.

travel.railway: Bathinda Junction railway station - about 3-5 km from this neighbourhood (verify).
travel.road: Hazura Kapura Colony / Shakti Vihar, Bathinda; reachable by auto/taxi within the city (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Navaratri periods are the main festive times (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Listed as 5:00 AM-9:00 PM daily in two sources (verify - small neighbourhood shrine, confirm locally).
